sn12.64:1.2: “Bhikkhus, there are these four kinds of nutriment for the maintenance of beings that have already come to be and for the assistance of those about to come to be.
sn12.64:1.4: The nutriment edible food, gross or subtle; second, contact; third, mental volition; fourth, consciousness.
sn12.64:1.5: These are the four kinds of nutriment for the maintenance of beings that have already come to be and for the assistance of those about to come to be.
sn12.64:2.1: “If, bhikkhus, there is lust for the nutriment edible food, if there is delight, if there is craving, consciousness becomes established there and comes to growth.
sn12.64:2.2: Wherever consciousness becomes established and comes to growth, there is a descent of name-and-form.
sn12.64:2.3: Where there is a descent of name-and-form, there is the growth of volitional formations.
sn12.64:2.4: Where there is the growth of volitional formations, there is the production of future renewed existence.
sn12.64:2.5: Where there is the production of future renewed existence, there is future birth, aging, and death.
sn12.64:2.6: Where there is future birth, aging, and death, I say that is accompanied by sorrow, anguish, and despair.
sn12.64:3.1: “If, bhikkhus, there is lust for the nutriment contact,
sn12.64:3.2: or for the nutriment mental volition,
sn12.64:3.3: or for the nutriment consciousness, if there is delight, if there is craving, consciousness becomes established there and comes to growth.
sn12.64:3.4: Wherever consciousness becomes established and comes to growth …
sn12.64:3.8: I say that is accompanied by sorrow, anguish, and despair.
sn12.64:4.1: “Suppose, bhikkhus, an artist or a painter, using dye or lac or turmeric or indigo or crimson, would create the figure of a man or a woman complete in all its features on a well-polished plank or wall or canvas.
sn12.64:4.2: So too, if there is lust for the nutriment edible food,
sn12.64:5.2: or for the nutriment mental volition,
sn12.64:5.3: or for the nutriment consciousness, if there is delight, if there is craving, consciousness becomes established there and comes to growth.
sn12.64:5.4: Wherever consciousness becomes established and comes to growth …
sn12.64:5.8: I say that is accompanied by sorrow, anguish, and despair.
sn12.64:6.1: “If, bhikkhus, there is no lust for the nutriment edible food,
sn12.64:7.2: or for the nutriment mental volition,
sn12.64:7.3: or for the nutriment consciousness, if there is no delight, if there is no craving, consciousness does not become established there and come to growth.
sn12.64:7.4: Where consciousness does not become established and come to growth, there is no descent of name-and-form.
sn12.64:7.5: Where there is no descent of name-and-form, there is no growth of volitional formations.
sn12.64:7.6: Where there is no growth of volitional formations, there is no production of future renewed existence.
sn12.64:7.7: Where there is no production of future renewed existence, there is no future birth, aging, and death.
sn12.64:7.8: Where there is no future birth, aging, and death, I say that is without sorrow, anguish, and despair.
sn12.64:8.1: “Suppose, bhikkhus, there was a house or a hall with a peaked roof, with windows on the northern, southern, and eastern sides. When the sun rises and a beam of light enters through a window, where would it become established?”
sn12.64:8.3: “If there were no western wall, where would it become established?”
sn12.64:8.5: “If there were no earth, where would it become established?”
sn12.64:8.7: “If there were no water, where would it become established?”
sn12.64:8.8: “It would not become established anywhere, venerable sir.”
sn12.64:8.9: “So too, bhikkhus, if there is no lust for the nutriment edible food …
sn12.64:9.3: for the nutriment consciousness … consciousness does not become established there and come to growth.
sn12.64:9.4: Where consciousness does not become established and come to growth …
sn12.64:9.8: … I say that is without sorrow, anguish, and despair.”
